about: English versions of the content imported from the old cushibir.org, written for the English site. Posts are keyed by slug; `paragraphs` follow the Bangla article paragraph by paragraph (null keeps the original, e.g. Arabic ayat). Load with `npm run seed:english`; safe to re-run. The branch should review statements before launch.

roktakt-julai-smorniy-rakhte-hobe.title: Bloody July: it must be remembered
roktakt-julai-smorniy-rakhte-hobe.excerpt: Time moves on. Much of the present becomes the past, and the future becomes the present; our eyes are always on the future. That is why we forget the past, and why that cruel past keeps coming back.
paragraphs: Bloody July: it must be remembered (Abu Talha Rafi; Department of Chemistry; session 2022-23;
University of Chittagong)
Time moves on. Much of the present becomes the past, and the future becomes the present; our eyes are always on the future. That is why we forget the past, and why that cruel past keeps coming back.

A present whose story holds the cruelty and barbarity of an autocratic ruler; the unchecked abuse and torture of a terrorist student organisation; the indiscriminate, hyena-like attacks of the autocrat's servile henchmen in the name of law enforcement; the silence of the so-called civil society; the opposition of teachers who should have been like fathers to us; bullets fired from helicopters; people made victims for speaking the truth: such a present, however far into the past it goes, can never be forgotten.

Those whose hands carry the blood of Abu Sayeed; who drained the fresh, young blood of some fifteen hundred talented, brave and spirited sons of the nation like Mugdho and Wasim; who took away the eyesight or the limbs of more than 30,000 of our brothers and sisters; at whose hands our mothers and sisters were humiliated: to forget them amid the concerns of the present would betray the blood of our martyred brothers. This past can never be forgotten.

Fighters of July: we must not let the bloody July of the past be hidden behind the many problems of the present or our hopes for the future, and we must not forget the bloodsuckers who have already taken so much blood. They must be stopped, and their venomous fangs broken by the full force of the law. Do not let them take advantage of any carelessness. They are blowing up small matters of the present to make us forget the past, trying to dim its memory by trapping you in a maze of present and future, so that they can find a way to live alongside you. Be careful, and always remember bloody July.....

islami-andolon-o-allahor-sathe-chukti.title: The Islamic movement and the covenant with Allah
islami-andolon-o-allahor-sathe-chukti.excerpt: "Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for Paradise" (Surah At-Tawbah, 111). What this verse means for the workers of the Islamic movement today.
paragraphs: Translation: Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth, in exchange for Paradise being theirs. They fight in the way of Allah, and they kill and are killed. It is a true promise binding on Him in the Torah, the Gospel and the Quran. (Surah At-Tawbah, 111)

This verse has a wide meaning for the workers of the Islamic movement. Allah the Exalted says He has purchased their lives and their wealth in exchange for Paradise. In other words, the very lives and wealth that Allah Himself gave, the Almighty now makes a covenant to buy, and in exchange for Paradise. This reward is only for those Muslims who accept the bargain.

If we think only about wealth, we need to know one basic feature of the Islamic economy: Allah alone owns all the wealth of the world, and people act only as its trustees. So why is Paradise declared the reward for giving wealth that already belongs to Allah? The answer lies in verse 155 of Surah Al-Baqarah.
Translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth, lives and fruits. And give good news to those who are patient.

In the Islamic movement there are workers who are ready to give their lives and a great deal of time but are unwilling to give their wealth. So what kind of wealth does Allah want? The answer is written in verse 92 of Surah Al Imran.
Translation: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love. And whatever you spend, Allah knows it well.
Now let us think a little about life. Sitting in the twenty-first century, what if we picture a person whose martyrdom does not stir society at all?

In a world with crewed aircraft that fly at almost seven times the speed of sound, where messages travel in a few milliseconds, where people of every culture meet on one platform within seconds, where artificial intelligence does complex work like data analysis in moments, where machines translate between many languages, and where a hydrogen bomb or a B83 nuclear bomb could wipe out a small country in an instant, if we ask whether the life of Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan or your life matters more to Allah, the difference in what a life is worth becomes plain. Such a question shows that the martyrdom of those who are skilled in technology, industry, literature, culture and the economy, and who take a special, leading role in them, is valued most by Allah.

Today it is essential for the workers of the Islamic movement to be skilled in every field of the times. The more they take the lead in different sectors at home and abroad, the more Allah will consider Muslims fit to govern the world. If the workers of the Islamic movement cannot shape their lives in the light of what the present age demands, their lives, or even their martyrdom, will not play a meaningful part in the Islamic movement.
Wahidul Islam
(Skills Development and Business Studies Secretary)

buk-ribhiuh-rasulullahor-sa-mokkar-jibon.title: Book review: The Makkan Life of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), by Maulana Motiur Rahman Nizami
buk-ribhiuh-rasulullahor-sa-mokkar-jibon.excerpt: When the path is lost in darkness and people have lost their way, the beloved Prophet (peace be upon him) came to this world like monsoon rain. This book is a lasting, poetic portrait of the seed of truth he sowed in the harsh desert of Makkah.
paragraphs: When the path is lost in darkness and people have lost their way, that is exactly when the beloved Prophet (peace be upon him) came to this world like a drop of monsoon rain. This book is a lasting, poetic portrait of the seed of truth he sowed, after prophethood, in the oppressed and persecuted hearts of that harsh Makkan desert. Across nine chapters and four stages, the author does not merely outline history; he paints a matchless philosophy of life for holding firm through the harshest adversity.

Turn the pages and those turbulent, thorny days of Makkah rise before your eyes: on one side the call to truth, on the other the ruthless plots of the Quraysh, the silent tears of the companions and the blood-soaked fields of Ta'if. Yet even amid so much darkness and pain, pictures of wisdom and love appear: the quiet night of the pledge of Aqabah, the bond of friendship with the people of Yathrib and, at last, by Allah's command, the hijrah to Madinah, leaving the home he had always known.

As Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said, "His character was the Quran." The author shows with great care how honesty, wisdom, trustworthiness and patience were in every speck of dust of those thirteen years in Makkah.

For those who are worn out by the storms of life today, whose steps falter again and again on the path of their ideals, whose hearts are shattered by the hostility of enemies or the loss of loved ones, this book will bring a gentle balm of faith to weary hearts. It will teach how, however long the darkness, one can stand firm by trusting in Allah, in sha Allah.
Borhan Uddin;
(Department of Anthropology

chobite-nishiddh-chhatrolig-o-jublig-kor.title: Banned Chhatra League and Jubo League activists hired as CU staff: Chhatrashibir condemns and protests
chobite-nishiddh-chhatrolig-o-jublig-kor.excerpt: Of the 12 third- and fourth-class staff approved at the 568th Syndicate meeting of the University of Chittagong, 3 are alleged to be linked to the banned Jubo League and Chhatra League, and all were hired from one particular area. Chhatrashibir's CU branch has strongly condemned and protested this.
paragraphs: Of the 12 third- and fourth-class staff whose appointments were approved at the 568th Syndicate meeting of the University of Chittagong, 3 are alleged to be linked to the banned organisations Jubo League and Chhatra League. In addition, all of the staff were hired from one particular area. Bangladesh Islami Chhatrashibir, University of Chittagong branch, has strongly condemned and protested this. Branch President Ibrahim Hossain Rony and Secretary Habib Ullah Khaled expressed the condemnation and protest in a joint statement.

The leaders said, "There is direct evidence that several of the 12 staff recently appointed at the University of Chittagong are involved with the banned organisations Chhatra League and Jubo League. The news that collaborators of fascism are once again being appointed on the campus of Shaheed Hridoy Tarua and Farhad, who lost their lives at the hands of the Awami fascists, has deeply saddened us. We strongly condemn and protest this."

The leaders also said, "In appointments at a public university there is no room for nepotism, regional influence, political identity or personal connections to come first. The only basis for appointment must be qualification, merit and the applicable rules. But we see a rush of appointments made only on the basis of the vice-chancellor's home area and party loyalty."

Calling on the university administration, the leaders said, "If there is any attempt to rehabilitate activists of a banned organisation on this campus, the successors of the martyrs will never accept it. Everyone connected with the League must be withdrawn at once, and all of the university's work must be run through a transparent and fair process, above regional favouritism and party identity."
Sent by:
Mehedi Hasan Sohan
Publicity Secretary,
Bangladesh Islami Chhatrashibir
University of Chittagong branch.

shotbhag-abason-abason-bhata-chaksu-o-si.title: Chhatrashibir's CU branch holds a press conference on five demands, including housing for every student, a housing allowance and CUCSU and Senate elections, and on Chhatra Dal's attempts to seize hall seats
shotbhag-abason-abason-bhata-chaksu-o-si.excerpt: Chhatrashibir's University of Chittagong branch held a press conference demanding housing for every student, a housing allowance, merit-based seat allocation through automation, transport reform and a roadmap for the next CUCSU and Senate elections, and on Chhatra Dal's recent attempts to seize seats.
paragraphs: Chhatrashibir's CU branch holds a press conference on five demands, including housing for every student, a housing allowance and CUCSU and Senate elections, and on Chhatra Dal's attempts to seize hall seats

Bangladesh Islami Chhatrashibir, University of Chittagong branch, has held a "press conference" demanding housing for every student, a housing allowance, merit-based seat allocation through an automated system, reform of transport and the publication of a roadmap for the next CUCSU and Senate elections, and on Chhatra Dal's recent attempts to seize seats.

The branch held the press conference today, Thursday 3 September, in front of the administrative building. It was moderated by branch Secretary Habib Ullah Khaled, and the written statement was read by branch President Ibrahim Hossain Rony.

In the written statement Ibrahim Hossain Rony said that the University of Chittagong was founded as a residential university. Yet almost six decades later, housing has still not been secured for most of its students. This is not only an administrative failure; it is a long-standing inequality in our education system and a real picture of students being denied a basic right.

Although it was founded in 1966, in 60 years the University of Chittagong has provided housing for less than 20 percent of its students. More than 80 percent are forced to live in unhealthy cottages and messes around the campus, or to pay high rents in the city.

Students have demanded housing for everyone from every administration since July. But the administration has still not given any specific roadmap for it. From today's press conference we officially raise the demand once again. We expect the university administration to present students with a clear roadmap for housing every student within the next 72 hours. At the same time, until that is achieved, urgent steps must be taken to introduce a housing allowance to ease the hardship of non-resident students.

He also said that, to keep the process free of political influence and nepotism, hall seats must be allocated only on merit through a fully automated process. Recently there have been reports of Chhatra Dal trying to seize seats illegally, and of seats in various halls being allotted to leaders and activists of one particular political party on the recommendation of senior figures in the administration. We say plainly: a hall seat is a basic right of students, and allocating seats fairly is one of the most important duties of the university administration. If the administration allots seats on political grounds instead of merit in order to favour anyone, we will be forced to take a firm stand against it.

He also said that the transport crisis is part of the housing crisis: because of the housing shortage, thousands of students have to live off campus, so it is the administration's duty to ensure safe and adequate transport for them. At a large residential university like the University of Chittagong, transport is not a luxury; it is an essential part of students' daily academic life. So alongside solving the housing problem, the transport system must be radically reformed.

On the seizure of seats he said: we are holding this press conference at a time when the housing crisis at the University of Chittagong is once again at the centre of discussion, and examples of Chhatra Dal spreading its political influence over hall seats have come to light. This deeply worries us. The last allotment under the fascist regime was in 2017. From the start of the fascist era, the now-banned Chhatra League seized seats step by step until it had illegally taken over every hall. Recently, provosts in several halls have again been opening the way to allocating seats illegally to favour one particular party. Where Chhatra Dal leaders cannot get what they want through a provost, they try to get it through threats and pressure, as students saw clearly in the case of the provost of Suhrawardy Hall who has just resigned. We strongly condemn this, and we clearly demand that the university administration quickly investigate the Chhatra Dal secretary's disgraceful conduct towards the provost and ensure justice.

Once a student's studentship ends, or if they are no longer a regular student, there can be no room to hold a residential seat for them because of their political identity. We want to make it clear that the halls of the University of Chittagong are for students; they will not be allowed to become a place to rehabilitate any political party's activists. We do not want to go back to the culture of the past, when political identity was the main qualification for a seat. Our position on seat allocation is very clear: seats must be allotted transparently, only on merit, through an automated process.
The written statement then set out five demands:
1. Housing must be ensured for every student.
2. Until housing for every student is ensured, a housing allowance must be introduced.
3. The transport system must be fully reformed.
4. Hall seats must be allocated on merit, with full transparency, through an automated process.
5. The schedule for the CUCSU and Senate elections must be announced immediately.

Also present were branch Office Secretary Rabiul Islam, Baitulmal Secretary Md. Ishaq Bhuiyan, International and Human Rights Secretary Saeed Bin Habib, Student Rights Secretary Monayem Sharif, Literature and Culture Secretary Hares Matabbar, Education Secretary Sajjat Hossain Munna and leaders at various levels.

bangladesh-islami-chhatroshibir-chottogr.title: Official website of Bangladesh Islami Chhatrashibir, University of Chittagong branch, launched
bangladesh-islami-chhatroshibir-chottogr.excerpt: The official website of CU Chhatrashibir, www.cushibir.org, was launched by central President Nurul Islam Saddam on 29 August 2026.
paragraphs: Official website of Bangladesh Islami Chhatrashibir, University of Chittagong branch, launched

The official website of the University of Chittagong branch of Chhatrashibir (CU Chhatrashibir) has been launched. The website (www.cushibir.org) was started to bring the organisation's work to students in a more organised, transparent and modern way.

On the evening of Saturday 29 August 2026, at the Mamun Memorial Library, Nurul Islam Saddam, central President of Bangladesh Islami Chhatrashibir, formally launched the official website of CU Chhatrashibir.

At the launch the central President said, "In today's age of information technology, the website will play an important role in bringing the organisation's activities, programmes, educational initiatives, notices, publications and other necessary information to students quickly and reliably. It will also help make the organisation's digital work more dynamic and up to date."

Branch President Ibrahim Hossain Rony said, "I hope this website will play a big part in closing the distance between the organisation and students, in increasing communication, feedback and advice, and in presenting the organisation's student welfare work."

Branch Secretary Habib Ullah Khaled said, "Information on the University of Chittagong branch's organisational and educational activities, programme updates, publications, news, notices and other information students need will be added to the website step by step."
Also present at the launch were Abu Musa, central Dawah Secretary of Bangladesh Islami Chhatrashibir, Mohammad Ibrahim, central Education Secretary, and other leaders of the branch.
CU Chhatrashibir said that new features and services will be added to the website to make technology-based services and communication easier for students.

chhatrodol-neta-nurul-huda-musa-hotyakan.title: Strong condemnation of the false accusation against Chhatrashibir over the killing of Chhatra Dal leader Nurul Huda Musa, and of dirty politics on campus
chhatrodol-neta-nurul-huda-musa-hotyakan.excerpt: Chhatrashibir's CU branch strongly condemns the attempt to blame it for the 1994 killing of Chhatra Dal leader Nurul Huda Musa, which happened off campus in infighting within CU Chhatra Dal, and to revive a 32-year-old false narrative to destabilise the campus.
paragraphs: Strong condemnation of the false accusation against Chhatrashibir over the killing of Chhatra Dal leader Nurul Huda Musa, and of dirty politics on campus

Bangladesh Islami Chhatrashibir, University of Chittagong branch, strongly condemns and protests the attempt to blame Chhatrashibir for the killing of Chhatra Dal leader Nurul Huda Musa, who died as a result of infighting within CU Chhatra Dal off campus in 1994, and to bring back a false narrative 32 years old in order to practise dirty politics and destabilise the campus.
In a joint statement, Ibrahim Hossain Rony and Habib Ullah Khaled, President and Secretary of the University of Chittagong branch of Chhatrashibir, strongly condemned and protested this attempt.

The leaders said, "Recently CU Chhatra Dal put up a banner at the campus Zero Point blaming Chhatrashibir for the killing of Chhatra Dal leader Nurul Huda Musa. It is creating confusion among ordinary students. Yet Chhatrashibir leaders and activists had not the slightest involvement in this killing.

According to various newspapers and informed people on campus at the time, Chhatra Dal leader Nurul Huda Musa was attacked off campus on 27 October 1994 in infighting between two Chhatra Dal groups, and died on 7 November that year while being treated at the military hospital in Dhaka. It is known that Nurul Huda Musa, organising secretary of the branch Chhatra Dal, was on hostile terms with another Chhatra Dal leader of the time, Titu, and his followers over control. Nurul Huda Musa was attacked as a result of their own infighting and died some days later.

The killing took place while the BNP government was in power. On his behalf, Iftekhar Hossain Mohsin, then president of the branch Chhatra Dal, filed a murder case at Hathazari police station against 8 people. After all legal proceedings in the case were completed, the full verdict was published in 2007. On the basis of the evidence, all of the accused were acquitted.

However, Chhatra Dal leaders and activists of the time spread the false accusation that Chhatrashibir had killed Nurul Huda Musa by cutting the tendons of his hands and feet, and made statements to various media, after which some outlets published reports. Capitalising on this false narrative, CU Chhatra Dal is now, 32 years later, again accusing Chhatrashibir and putting up banners in an attempt to practise dirty politics on campus.

Speaking with the lawyers involved in the case, we learned that there is no mention of cut tendons anywhere in the case filing, the medical report or the post-mortem report. We openly challenge CU Chhatra Dal to present proper evidence for its claim.

The BNP government was in power when Nurul Huda Musa was killed, and although the BNP returned to power in 2001, it did not ensure a proper trial for the killing. But now, 32 years later, Chhatra Dal wants to create a violent situation on campus by deliberately blaming Chhatrashibir for it. We strongly condemn and protest such shameful conduct, and call on them to present proper evidence for their claim. Otherwise we will be forced to take legal action against the Chhatra Dal leaders for damaging the reputation of Islami Chhatrashibir."
Sent by:
Mehedi Hasan Sohan
Publicity Secretary
Bangladesh Islami Chhatrashibir
University of Chittagong branch

shohid-mir-mugdhor-name-oyatar-kornar-st.title: CU Shibir sets up a water corner named after Shaheed Mir Mugdho
shohid-mir-mugdhor-name-oyatar-kornar-st.excerpt: Two drinking-water filters named after Shaheed Mir Mugdho of the July uprising, at the Zero Point and the Shaheed Minar.
paragraphs: The University of Chittagong (CU) branch of Chhatrashibir has installed two drinking-water filters named after Shaheed Mir Mugdho, who was martyred in the July mass uprising.

The water corner at the university's Shaheed Minar was opened at 12 noon on Tuesday (21 October) by branch Chhatrashibir President Mohammad Ali. Branch General Secretary Mohammad Parvez and other leaders were present.

The organisation said two drinking-water filters have been installed, at the university's Zero Point and at the Shaheed Minar. They were due to be installed during the CUCSU election but were held back because of the code of conduct. Students will benefit from having filters at these two important places on campus.
Sabiha Yasmin, a student of the Department of History, said happily, "The water quality is very good. A filter at the central point will help us a lot. Thanks to Chhatrashibir for this."
